Document error subclasses

Source: R/aaa-doc_errors.R
doc_errors.Rd

These internal helpers build the list of error subclasses in the @returns section of a function's documentation. Include man/rmd/error-classes.md as a child chunk to introduce the list, then call .doc_errors() in a roxygen R chunk (with results = "asis" and echo = FALSE) with one or more .doc_err*() entries. .doc_errors() sorts the entries alphabetically by subclass and errors if a subclass is documented more than once.

Usage

.doc_errors(...)

.doc_err(subclass, text)

.doc_err_other(text)

.doc_err_null(arg = "allow_null")

.doc_err_na()

.doc_err_named()

.doc_err_allowed_names()

.doc_err_named_fn()

.doc_err_empty(fn = NULL)

.doc_err_scalar(fn = NULL)

.doc_err_size(
  what = "vector",
  min = "min_size",
  max = "max_size",
  fn = NULL,
  x_vs_y = TRUE
)

.doc_err_size_x_vs_y(
  min = "min_size",
  max = "max_size",
  also = NULL,
  fn = NULL
)

.doc_err_n_characters(scalar = FALSE)

.doc_err_regex()

.doc_err_tz(when = NULL)

.doc_err_range(exclusive = FALSE)

.doc_err_allowed_values(scalar = FALSE)

.doc_err_unique()

.doc_err_function()

.doc_err_fct_levels()

.doc_err_multiple_of()

.doc_err_not_multiple(scalar = FALSE)

.doc_err_coerce(class_name, description = class_name, extra = NULL)

.doc_err_incompatible(
  class_name,
  description = class_name,
  what = c("values", "elements")
)

Arguments

...

.doc_err*() entries (or lists of entries).

subclass

(character) The error subclass, as passed to .stbl_abort() (for example, "bad_named" or c("coerce", "character")), without the "stbl-error-" prefix.

text

(character(1)) The description, starting with "when" or "for" and ending with a period. For .doc_err_other(), the full bullet text.

arg

(character(1)) The name of the argument that controls the check.

fn

(character(1)) Optional name of the function (without parentheses) to mention, for entries that only apply to one function.

what

(character(1)) What can't be converted: "values" (the default) or "elements" (for list inputs).

min, max

(character(1)) Names of the arguments that bound the size.

x_vs_y

(logical(1)) Whether to include the size_x_vs_y entry.

also

(character(2)) Optional second pair of min and max argument names for size_x_vs_y.

scalar

(logical(1)) Whether the entry describes a single value rather than a vector.

when

(character(1)) Optional condition that must hold before tz is checked.

exclusive

(logical(1)) Whether the range also has exclusive bounds.

class_name

(character(1)) The name of the target class as used in the subclass (for example, "integer").

description

(character(1)) The description of the target class as used in the text (defaults to class_name).

extra

(character(1)) Optional text appended to the description.

Value

.doc_err*() return an entry for .doc_errors(). .doc_errors() returns markdown.

Details

Entries that share wording across many functions have their own helper (for example, .doc_err_null()). Helpers for the coerce and incompatible_values subclasses take the target class so the subclass and text stay consistent. Use .doc_err() for one-off entries and .doc_err_other() for entries that don't correspond to an stbl subclass.
